title.zh: 海底裂開的那一刻：科學家首次親眼見證大洋中脊的「產房時刻」
title.en: When the Seafloor Split Open: Scientists Witness a Mid-Ocean Ridge Birth for the First Time

summary.zh:
【總結】

2024年，印度洋東南印度洋中脊的一段，經歷了一場罕見的海底擴張事件——而人類首次用科學儀器完整記錄了它。研究團隊在阿姆斯特丹島附近部署了一個臨時海底觀測站，就在安裝四個月後，這個觀測站捕捉到了約四公尺的海底沉降與超過一公尺的水平伸展，隨後約一百五十萬立方公尺的岩漿湧上海底，形成新的洋殼。這項研究不僅是海洋地質學史上的里程碑，更讓科學家第一次看清了「板塊張開」的完整過程：從岩漿房收縮、岩脈侵入、斷層滑移，到岩漿噴發，每一個環節都清晰可辨。

【研究問題】

海底擴張是塑造地球表面最重要的地質過程之一，但發生在數公里深的海底，長期以來人類只能靠間接推測來理解它。陸地上的大地震可以用GPS和衛星影像直接測量地殼變形，但海水會吸收電磁波，讓這些技術在海底完全失效。過去幾十年，科學家在中洋脊區域只能觀察到火山活動的痕跡，卻無法同時捕捉變形與地震的細節，更不知道這些過程的比例如何分配——尤其是「無震滑移」到底佔了多少。解決這個問題，不僅能揭示板塊運動的真實機制，也能回答一個長期爭議：為什麼中洋脊的變形速率很快，釋放的震能卻相對稀少？

【研究方法】

研究團隊在東南印度洋中脊的I1段部署了一套多學科整合的海底觀測網絡，包含四種關鍵設備：一是水聽器陣列，用於偵測和定位海底地震以及岩漿噴發時產生的聲學信號；二是橫向聲學測距儀陣列，架設在擴張段兩側，能以毫米級精度測量海底水平位移；三是自校準海底壓力計，監測海底垂直方向的抬升或沉降；四是重複船載多波束測深，在事件前後繪製海底地形變化。研究團隊還結合了全球地震目錄（GCMT）的震源機制數據，並用彈性變形數值模型反推岩漿房收縮與斷層滑移的量級。這種多源數據融合的方式，讓研究者得以重建整個事件的時序與物理機制。

【結果】

研究揭示了完整的擴張事件序列：首先，一系列地震沿著中洋脊軸向遷移，伴隨約四公尺的階梯式海底沉降，這與岩漿房（岩床）排空有關；接著，聲學測距儀記錄到脊軸以西的基線伸長了0.5至1.5公尺，顯示水平伸展正在發生；最後，約一百五十萬立方公尺的岩漿噴發到海底，形成了數公尺厚的熔岩流，這個體積與2015年Axial海底火山爆發相當。更關鍵的發現是：此次事件中，斷層滑移的幾何矩遠大於地震釋放的震源矩，推估約75%的斷層滑移是無震的。這意味著中洋脊的板塊分離主要靠「安靜的滑動」完成，而非頻繁的地震——這一結論可能徹底改變我們對全球中洋脊系統變形機制的理解。
summary.en:
**Summary:**

In 2024, a segment of the Southeast Indian Ridge near Amsterdam Island experienced a rare seafloor spreading event—and for the first time in history, scientists captured its full anatomy. A temporary seafloor observatory, deployed just four months earlier, recorded approximately four meters of axial valley subsidence and over one meter of horizontal extension, followed by roughly 1.5 million cubic meters of magma erupting onto the seafloor. This landmark study offers an unprecedented, step-by-step view of seafloor spreading: from magma chamber deflation and dike intrusion, to aseismic and seismic fault slip, and finally to volcanic eruption. It transforms a process that was once inferred indirectly into one that has been directly observed and quantified.

**Problem:**

Seafloor spreading is Earth's primary mechanism for creating new oceanic crust, yet it occurs kilometers beneath the sea surface, shielded from the GPS and satellite techniques that have revolutionized our understanding of terrestrial earthquakes. For decades, mid-ocean ridges have been studied almost exclusively through earthquake catalogs and shipboard bathymetry, both of which lack the resolution to capture the millimeter- to meter-scale deformation that accompanies spreading. A key unanswered question is the degree to which extension at mid-ocean ridges is seismic versus aseismic—why do these rapidly deforming boundaries release so little seismic energy? Resolving this requires direct, simultaneous measurements of deformation and seismicity, something that has never been achieved at an oceanic spreading center until now.

**Approach:**

The researchers deployed a multi-instrument seafloor observatory on the I1 segment of the Southeast Indian Ridge, combining four complementary measurement systems. Hydrophone arrays detected and located underwater earthquakes and captured impulsive H-waves—acoustic signals generated by lava-seawater interaction during the eruption. Horizontal acoustic ranging instruments, positioned on either side of the ridge axis, measured seafloor displacement with millimeter-level precision. A self-calibrating bottom pressure recorder monitored vertical deformation of the axial valley floor. After the event, ship-based multibeam bathymetry mapped the seafloor again, revealing the extent and volume of newly emplaced lava flows. The team integrated these observations with global centroid moment tensor (GCMT) data and used elastic dislocation modeling to invert for the contributions of magma intrusion, dike opening, and fault slip—allowing them to reconstruct the event's full mechanical sequence.

**Results:**

The study documented a cascading sequence of events: a swarm of earthquakes migrated along the ridge axis and into adjacent transform faults, accompanied by approximately four meters of stepwise subsidence in the axial valley, consistent with deflation of a shallow magma lens. Acoustic ranging revealed 0.5 to 1.5 meters of horizontal extension west of the ridge axis. Subsequent eruption extruded roughly 1.5 million cubic meters of lava—comparable in volume to the 2015 Axial Seamount eruption. The most striking finding is the seismic moment deficit: the geometric moment inferred from fault slip models far exceeds the seismic moment released by earthquakes, implying that approximately 75 percent of the normal faulting during this event was aseismic. This suggests that the majority of plate separation at mid-ocean ridges may occur through silent, aseismic slip rather than earthquakes—a finding with profound implications for how we understand deformation across global ridge systems.

keyArticle.title: Anatomy of a seafloor spreading event captured by in situ seismogeodesy
